title: Charged particles in uniform electric fields; Particle accelerators and detectors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: F05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; P04-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; P04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; P04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: F05-1#N.3, P04-1#N.3, F05-1#N.5a, P04-1#N.5, F05-1#N.14, P04-1#N.12, P04-1#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Weight
items.clue: Pull of gravity: about 10⁻²⁹ N on an electron, so negligible here.

items.label: Focusing magnets
items.clue: Components that keep the beam narrow as it travels round the ring.

items.label: Bending magnets
items.clue: Components that curve the path of the particles so that they stay on the ring.

items.label: Accelerating cavities
items.clue: Regions where an alternating electric field gives the particles energy on each lap.

questions.stem: Two horizontal parallel plates, 2.5 cm apart in a vacuum, have a potential difference of 150 V between them. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of an electron between the plates? Gravity is negligible. Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.
A proton crosses 20 gaps in a linac. The pd across each gap is 50 kV as the proton crosses it. How much kinetic energy does the proton gain?
questions.explanation: Each gap gives charge × V = e × 50 kV = 50 keV. 20 × 50 keV = 1000 keV = 1.0 MeV (1.6 × 10⁻¹³ J).

questions.stem: Two parallel plates, 2.0 cm apart in a vacuum, have a potential difference of 500 V between them. An electron is released from rest at the negative plate and accelerates across the gap. What is its speed when it reaches the positive plate? Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.
A cyclotron accelerates protons with a fixed magnetic field. It is now used for alpha particles: twice the charge, about four times the mass. What must happen to the frequency of the alternating pd?

options.text: It must be doubled, because the alpha particle has twice the charge.
It can stay the same, because the time per half-turn does not depend on speed.
It must be quartered, because the alpha particle is four times as heavy.

questions.explanation: The frequency is proportional to charge ÷ mass. 2 ÷ 4 = ½, so each half-turn takes twice as long.

questions.stem: A proton and an alpha particle are placed, one at a time, at the same point in a uniform electric field. The alpha particle has twice the charge of the proton and about four times its mass. Gravity is negligible. What is the ratio (acceleration of the alpha particle) / (acceleration of the proton)?
questions.explanation: Correct. Acceleration = charge × E ÷ mass, so the ratio is (2/4) = 1/2. The alpha particle accelerates half as much.

questions.stem: In a detector with a uniform magnetic field, a V of two tracks starts from one point. Both products have the same size of charge. One track has a much larger radius of curvature than the other. What does this show?

options.text: The particle with the larger radius had more momentum.
The particle with the larger radius had more charge.
The particle with the larger radius was neutral.
The two particles had the same momentum but different masses.

questions.explanation: r = p/BQ. Same B and same size of Q, so the larger radius means the larger p.

questions.stem: A ring's bending magnets already run at their maximum field. Engineers want protons with three times the momentum. What must they do?

options.text: Build a ring with nine times the bending radius, since kinetic energy goes as momentum squared.
Build a smaller ring, since faster protons are easier to steer.
Build a ring with three times the bending radius.
Keep the ring and add more accelerating cavities.

questions.explanation: Radius = momentum ÷ (B × charge). B cannot rise, so the radius must rise in proportion: three times the momentum, three times the radius.
